background: SEB is a Swedish universal bank with a corporate and institutional focus, funded by Swedish and Baltic deposits and covered bonds and lending to large Nordic corporates, Swedish households and businesses in the Baltic states.
synthesis: Ratings are among the highest in Europe: AA on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at AA-, all three on a stable outlook, after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is mixed against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 17.2% is above the peer median, while leverage of 5.1% is below it. Liquidity is the weak side, with LCR of 125% and NSFR of 110% both in the bottom quarter, though none of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods to 30 Jun 2026. Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days: very high ratings and sound capital, with liquidity ratios at the low end for a bank of its grade.
